sentences.text: The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 20.04.2024 at about 1.20 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in Auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB- 6163 at Batavadi Circle, NH-73 Tumkur.
At that time the driver of said auto rickshaw drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and has topple the vehicle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Adithya Orthopedic and Truma Center, Tumkur wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

entities.text: Adithya Orthopedic and Truma Center, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and she was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that she has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
She is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, she was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years as on the date of accident.
She was working Product Consultant, Zugang Manpowers India Pvt., Ltd., Tumkur and was earning Rs.21,670/- per month.
She was maintaining her family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to her family.
Due to the accidental injuries she could not able to do any kind of work compared to her previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on her earning capacity and as such herself and her family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent No.1, who drive his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB-6163.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said vehicle

thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.2 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
7.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till realization.

Nagashree H vs Aftab Ahamed on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76196862/
2 8.
After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
In pursuance of service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and have filed their written statement by denying the entire petition averments.
The respondents have pleaded that the insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age of the petitioner, avocation, income, injuries sustained, treatment underwent by the petitioner, disability certificate obtained by the petitioner,
medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
9. In order to substantiate her claim, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
In addition to her evidence, the petitioner got examined the medical record Department as PW.2.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
Even after giving sufficient opportunity to respondent to lead the respondent evidence, the respondents have not turned up before this court to lead the same.

Hence, after giving sufficient opportunities to respondents to lead the respondent evidence, the respondent evidence was taken as nil and case was posted for arguments.
10.
Heard the arguments on both side and perused the materials on record.

11. Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB- 6163 by its driver, in RTA took place on 20.04.2024 at about 1.20 p.m., on NH-73 Road, Batawadi Circle, Tumkur Town?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
12. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative

,
 Issue No.3 :

As per the final orders  for the following:-

sentences.text: The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 20.04.2024 at about 1.20 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in Auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB-6163 at Batavadi Circle, NH- 73 Tumkur.
At that time the driver of said auto rickshaw drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and has topple the vehicle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to various parts of body.

14. The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
15. By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 17 documents in total on her behalf.
Further, PW.1 has got marked 13 documents on her behalf as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.

Further,
the petitioner got examined the Medical Record Department, Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Center, Tumkur, Hospital, as PW.2 has got marked 4 documents as per Ex.P14 to Ex.P.17.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Center, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In his chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offender vehicle.
16. The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent No.1.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
17. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR and complaint, Ex.P.2 is the crime detail form, Ex.P.3 is the spot sketch, Ex.P.4 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
18. The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1 offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-AB-6163.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by her.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance Nagashree H vs Aftab Ahamed on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76196862/
4 allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.
(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-

In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate which are marked as per Ex.P.5.
As per the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
The Ex.P.8 is the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital from 20.04.2024 to 21.04.2024 for a period of 2 days.
These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Center Hospital, Tumkur, but the doctor is not examined by petitioner.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Without the examination of the doctor it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

Further to prove the nature of his injuries the petitioner has examined one Lakshminarasaiah, Medical Record Department at Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur, as PW.2, through him, authorization letter, MLC extract, case sheet and x-ray which are marked under Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.17.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur.

entities.text: Aditya Orthopedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Without the evidence of doctor towards assessment of disability it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

In number of Judgments delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court it is highlighted that i) In a motor vehicle accident case, where a doctor was not examined court may award "global compensation" which is typically a lower amount due to the lack of concrete medical evidence to support the extent of injuries often resulting in a reduced compensation package compared to cases with proper medical documentation.
Due to lack of crucial medical evidence from the doctors only covers minimal damages or pain and sufferings.

ii). Courts may reason that without a proper medical examination, it is difficult to accurately assess the extent of the disability and the resulting loss of income or future prospectus leading to a lower over all compensation award.
iii). Even if a doctor was not examined, the court may still consider the visible injuries or the severity of the accident when determining the compensation amount.

Nagashree H vs Aftab Ahamed on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76196862/
5 iv).
The court may rely on the claimant's own testimony regarding their injuries and limitations but this may be less persuasive without supporting medical evidence.

v). Some cases has seen tribunals award a nominal compensation amount such as a few thousand rupees, when a claimant failed to present a doctor's examination report, highlighting the importance of medical documentation in such cases.
vi) Not examining the doctor significantly weakens the plaintiff's case as it make it difficulty to establish the standard of care that was breached and the patient's injury.

vii) The plaintiff bears the burden of proving medical negligence and failing to examine the treating doctor can make it challenging to meet this standard.
viii) Several Indian Court cases have highlighted the issue of not examining the treating doctor, resulting in significantly reduced compensation awards.
ix) Even if a court does award compensation, the amount will likely be lower due to factors like the severity of the injury, availability of other medical evidence and the plaintiff's contribution to the situation.
In Sunitha V/s Rajasthan State Transport Corporation dated 15.02.2019 Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that, non examination of "best witness" in motor accident claim cases is not fatal and also not to find fault with non examination of some best witnesses.
Applying the above principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court to the case on hand it is observed that though non examination of the doctor by the petitioner is not fatal to the case but without the assessment of the disability by the doctor it is impossible to believe that the petitioner has sustained the injuries narrated in the petition.

sentences.text: Thereby the petitioner is not entitled to compensation towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a Product Consultant at Zugang Manpowers India Pvt., Ltd., Tumkur and used to earn Rs.21,670/- per month.

In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month.

the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.33,000/- (30 days X 550 = Rs.16,500 + 16,500).

6 reliance on medical bills.

(C) Future medical expenditure
The petitioner has not claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
Therefore the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under this head.
(D) Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 2 days with extended follow up treatment.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance to meet the treatment.
Wound certificate Ex.P5 shows injuries and patient would have received help from family members are friends to get admitted at the hospital.
In Pradeep B. Siddarameshwara v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Dated:10.12.2014

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that "on account of non-examination of doctor and assessment of disability by doctor being not available on record, Tribunal has proceeded to award global compensation of Rs.3,000/-, which is abysmally on the lower side.

Considering the fact that claimant had sustained fracture of left ring finger and due to same he has undergone pain and suffering, this Court is of the considered view that additional compensation of Rs.20,000/-, if awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

Said additional global compensation is awarded taking into consideration the nature of injury, which covers the head of 'loss of income daring laid up period', 'pain and suffering', 'loss of amenities' and disability that has been sustained by claimant."

In Devaraju V/s Sharad Sharma dated: 15.03.2011 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that "Material submissions probabalise, accident is not disputed actionable negligence is not disputed, wound certificate is marked.
Wound certificate reflects two fractures.
It is believed by the tribunal.

It is not the quantum of evidence,
it is quality is the criteria.
Compensation awarded at Rs. 12,000/- is on lesser side.

So it is enhanced to global amount of Rs.
40,000/- difference of Rs. 28,000/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit"
Therefore in absence of proof, it would be reasonable to award conveyance charges,
attendance and special diet of Rs.25,000/- each.
In total the petitioner is entitle for Rs.75,000/- under this head.

(a) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
Nagashree H vs Aftab Ahamed on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76196862/
7
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained injuries as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused lot of pain to suffer in the future life span.
Pain and suffering would be categorized as a non-pecuniary loss as it is incapable of being arithmetically calculated.

Therefore, when compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering, special circumstances of the claimant have to be taken into account including the victim's age, the unusual deprivation the victim has suffered, the effect thereof on his or her future life.

Like wise, in the case of Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Devaraju V/s Sharad Sharma dated: 15.03.2011 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177 the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above formula to the case on hand and by considering the nature of the injuries caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
This includes a variety of matters such as the inability to walk, run or sit, etc.
This shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of the personal life and amenities of life.

In T.Murthy V/s Zabiulla Dated 08.01.2016 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has opined that "I find that the tribunal has committed an error in not considering Ex.P.8 wound certificate and non examination of doctor.
For having suffered grievous injury in the road accident which has been proved before the tribunal, I am inclined to grant another Rs.25,000/- global compensation".
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Conveyance allowance, Rs. 75,000/-
 attendant charge and  special diet Nagashree H vs Aftab Ahamed on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76196862/

8  6 Pain and sufferings Rs. 1,00,000/-
 7 Loss of enjoyment and loss Rs. 30,000/-
 of amenities of life  Total Rs. 2,51,402/-
 Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.2,51,402/- which is just and proper.
21. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,51,402/-, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in her favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
